Alyssa — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. High level first, then Dev will follow up with the micro tradeoffs: 

1) Primary recommendation: H100-focused fleet for latency-critical, high-context clinical models. Rationale: H100 gives the best mix of large HBM (80GB/94GB variants), Tensor Core throughput, and multi-instance flexibility for model parallelism. For 48k-token context models we expect persistent KV/cache needs and HBM is the simplest way to avoid frequent off-device caching.

2) Secondary/fallback: a split between A100 (80GB) for steady-state resilience and L4 for non-latency workloads. Use A100 as the lower-cost option for serving smaller-context (<=16k) variants and as a warm-failover when H100 pools are at capacity. L4 is attractive for batching/embeddings and large-scale offline jobs.

3) NVLink / multi-GPU: If you plan to shard a single inference request across GPUs for the 48k models, co-locate into NVLink domains (same host / same NVSwitch) to reduce cross-host PCIe hops. If you instead run quantized 8-bit variants, you can avoid sharding for many model checkpoints — we'll include quantization guidance in Dev's note.

4) Operational mix suggestion (initial POC 40-GPU equivalent baseline): 
   - 60% H100 (8 x H100 logical instances) for latency-critical online traffic
   - 30% A100 (to handle mid-priority LLMs and warm failover)
   - 10% L4 (batch embeddings + nightly ingestion)

I'll attach a short SLA/latency scenario doc and we've asked Dev for a per-SKU cost/perf matrix. Can we sync on a 30-min call Monday to lock the MA Plan for procurement?

—Jordan

Alyssa / team — digging into specifics below, focusing on the three SKUs and the concrete memory/perf tradeoffs you asked about. TL;DR at the top.

TL;DR: H100 (preferred) for large-context, low-p95 latency; A100 (good) when cost/throughput is primary; L4 (best price-per-embedding) for high-throughput non-interactive jobs.

Technical notes:
- Memory footprint: H100 80GB/94GB allows single-GPU serving for many 7B-70B style LLMs with large context windows when using KV offload/partial sharding. For 48k token windows on 70B-class clinical models we estimate peak working set ~40–60GB after GPT-style KV overhead depending on tokenization — H100 margins are safest. A100-80GB can work but requires tighter KV caching and possibly model parallel split for worst-case sequences. L4 (24GB) is not suitable for those 48k-context online flows unless you run aggressive quantization + recomposition (and accept increased p95 latency).
- Throughput vs latency: H100 provides the best single-request p95 due to higher FP/INT throughput; A100 is close for steady smaller contexts. L4 throughput is high for batched embeddings but per-request token p95 will be worse for interactive.
- Quantization: We recommend a mixed strategy. Keep highest-fidelity checkpoints on H100 (no/low quant), run int8/4-bit quantized variants on A100 for many RLHF/few-shot assistants, and put quantized embedding models on L4. We'll validate each checkpoint in our Optimize pipeline.
- Sharding & NVLink: If you must exceed single-HBM capacity, prefer NVSwitch-backed nodes (NVLink) for model parallelism; this reduces host-to-host hops and keeps token latency within your p95 target. Without NVLink, you should prefer logical sharding with careful batching to avoid p95 spikes.
- Autoscaling and burst: Plan an asynchronous burst pool (A100-heavy + L4) for queued/throughput work and a reserved H100 pool for critical low-latency flows. Configure Redwood Dedicated to route by policy: latency-first -> H100, cost-first -> A100/L4.

Cost considerations: H100 cost per GPU-hour is materially higher. We modelled three scenarios in the attached spreadsheet: "latency-optimized", "balanced", "cost-optimized". For your projected load, balanced gives ~18% lower cost vs full H100 while keeping >95% of low-latency coverage.

I'll run a quick validation job on your spreadsheet to produce an explicit GPU-hour run-rate and per-token cost for the POC. Expect that attachment in an hour.

—Dev

Alyssa — consolidating the recommended MA plan and procurement asks for your vendor team / procurement packet: 

1) Recommended initial fleet for POC (capacity expressed as GPU-equivalent slots):
   - 24 H100 slots (primary, reserved)
   - 12 A100 slots (warm failover + mid-priority serving)
   - 4 L4 slots (batch embeddings / ingestion)

2) Operational SLAs & runbook excerpts to include in SOW:
   - Latency objective: H100-backed routes p95 <= 120ms for token generation under expected concurrency (profile attached in latency_sla_scenarios.pdf)
   - Failover: automatic routing to A100 within 30s on H100 degradation, with capacity-based throttling to preserve stability.
   - Autoscale burst: L4/A100 pool cold-start to warm pool target 10–15m (policy-driven).

3) Procurement items: network egress limits, NVLink-enabled instance SKUs for sharded runs, and a two-stage acceptance test (workload replay + live traffic shadow run).

Next steps: Jordan/Marissa — can you confirm contract language for reserved burst capacity and a 90-day canary window for model rollouts (we typically put runtime canary rollback triggers in the SOW)? Alyssa — once procurement confirms PO timing we'll firm the exact counts and a migration checklist.

—Rishi
